key_insight: A small set of real measurements can validate a high-fidelity FEM model, which then generates enough synthetic data to train a real-time GNN surrogate for soft tactile deformation.
engineering_relevance: This enables sub-millimeter tactile deformation prediction at millisecond speed, supporting virtual prototyping and simulator-based design without extensive fragile-sensor testing.
method: Validate an ANSYS FEM model using 82 camera-tracked real contact cases.
Generate 768 synthetic contact scenarios from the validated FEM for GNN training.
Use the GNN for both forward prediction and inverse inference of tactile deformation/contact localization.
evidence_signal: The validated FEM achieved sub-0.5 mm error in over 90% of validation cases, and the GNN reached 0.32 mm mean absolute error with millisecond inference on the tested planar tactile structure.
watch_item: Results are demonstrated on a 2D planar tactile setup, so transfer to more complex 3D sensors or unseen material behaviors may require revalidation.
paper_title: FEM-Validated Real-Time Modelling of Soft Tactile Deformation
